Source: http://www.nationalpost.com

Posted September 26, 2000
(MarijuanaNews note: Canadian politicians have been trying to defuse the marijuana part of the drug prohibition issue in the wake of the remarkable series of articles by the Ottawa Citizen’s Dan Gardner.
See
We Are Winning! Canadian Conservative Alliance Leader Calls for Parliamentary Debate on Legalization of Drugs! Members from All Parties Back Proposal, But Government Follows DEAland.
Last week the official government response indicated an acceptance of " decriminalization " of personal possession -- meaning that a small fine, rather than jail time, would be the worst possible punishment.
See
Canadian Government’s Mindless Response to Ottawa Citizen Series on Prohibition Seems to Indicate Acceptance of " Decriminalization " of Marijuana.

Here Allan Rock, the Canadian Health Minister, is promising that something will be done about medical marijuana " by this time next year. " He is expanding on an even less coherent press release from Health Canada.
See
Health Canada Press Release Makes Clear that the Health of Canadians Is Less Important than Marijuana Prohibition. Victimization of a Patient Gives More Proof.

The bad news is that he seems locked into a bureaucratic mindset on the ultimate model for medical marijuana. The good news is that – in the meantime -- he wants " the police to ‘use discretion’ when dealing with people who supply marijuana to medical users. " In other words, until he can take over the medical marijuana business, he will leave the compassion clubs alone. Of course, in most of Canada, and especially in Vancouver, the police are well ahead of him.

He also seems to be signaling that marijuana will be " decriminalized " by administrative action under the " Contraventions Act " -- a federal statute that allows provincial and federal offences to be dealt with by tickets and fines, rather than criminal charges.

In short, the leaders of Canada are cautiously following the people. This is at least better than DEAland in which the leaders do everything possible to deceive the people, and then ignore them, when that fails.)

September 25, 2000
From The National Post
letters@nationalpost.com
http://www.nationalpost.com/commentary.asp?s2=letters
http://www.nationalpost.com/
http://forums.canada.com/~nationalpost
By Luiza Chwialkowska
OTTAWA WILL GROW, SUPPLY POT FOR USE BY THE SICK: ROCK
Health Canada Will Select Official Supplier Soon
See
In Canada Only the Government Has Difficulty Getting Marijuana.
However, " Canadians who want to take part in a clinical trial
will find application forms on Health Canada’s Web Site "

Allan Rock, the federal Minister of Health, says, " The day may come when marijuana is available on pharmacists' shelves. "

OTTAWA - A government-controlled supply of marijuana will be grown and federal regulations governing medicinal use will be made into law within a year, according to Allan Rock, the Minister of Health.

" The day may come when marijuana is available on pharmacists' shelves, " predicted Mr. Rock in an interview.

Health Canada will select an official marijuana supplier over the next month or two and the supply will be available depending on " how long after that it will take them to produce the first crop, dry it, cut it, and [laughs] ... roll it, " he said.

While the department develops its supply, Mr. Rock has appealed to police to " use discretion " when dealing with people who supply marijuana to medical users.

Mr. Rock is also eager for a Cabinet discussion decriminalizing possession of small amounts of marijuana, he said.

But the debate must be launched by Anne McLellan, the Minister of Justice.

" There's no doubt that it's something she and I should talk about. And Cabinet would probably want to be involved in the decision. But we look to the Minister of Justice to take the lead in relation to the question of whether any offence should be added to the Contraventions Act, " said Mr. Rock.

" I'd be happy to participate fully in a vigorous Cabinet discussion on that issue -- whenever she brings that to the table, " he said.

The Contraventions Act is a federal statute that lists provincial and federal offences that are dealt with by tickets and fines, rather than criminal charges.

" Think of the difference between being charged with speeding, or being charged with dangerous driving, " said Mr. Rock.

" The issue is should the possession of small amounts of marijuana be subject to a ticketable offence rather than criminal charges?

" We're watching an evolution here from complete prohibition, " he said. " Maybe someday [recreational users] will be given a ticket. "
(MarijuanaNews note: We are watching the Canadian political class carefully retreat from marijuana prohibition. This is a strategic maneuver, not enlightenment.)
See
We Are Winning! Support Grows for Full Legalization of Marijuana in Canada.

A spokeswoman for Ms. McLellan has said the Justice Minister considers marijuana policy to be a matter of health policy.
(MarijuanaNews note: She seems to be ducking the issue.)
See
Great Canadian Editorial Calls for Legalization; Decries Justice Minister's Giving Narks Veto Over Changing Marijuana Laws.

" Having served for four years as the Attorney-General of Canada, I can tell you that is an issue for the Attorney-General of Canada and the Minister of Justice, " said Mr. Rock.

To date, Mr. Rock has granted 72 exemptions to patients suffering from AIDS, cancer, epilepsy, and other conditions doctors believe can be helped by the drug.

But the Ontario Court of Appeal has ruled that without formal rules, the process is too arbitrary, secretive, and allows Mr. Rock too much discretion.

" What the court said to us is we shouldn't innovate. We shouldn't just play it by ear ... Carve it into law so everybody knows where they stand, " he said.
See
Canadian Court Says Lack of Provision for Medical Marijuana Violates Fundamental Rights; Gives Parliament 12 Months to Fix Marijuana Prohibition -- Or There Will Be No Marijuana Laws in Canada.

" At this time next year, there will be a set of regulations on the shelf that will spell out who is allowed to apply for medical marijuana, how the application is made, what the requirements are, what the criteria are that the minister must take into account in deciding, how and within what period of time the minister will communicate a decision, " he said.
(MarijuanaNews note: This indicates that he intends to try to keep control over access to medical marijuana. That will not fly. In Canada, doctors can prescribe heroin, albeit with some more restrictions than morphine.)

 " And within a year, if you are granted an exemption for medical marijuana, you will be able to collect it from Health Canada. It will be clear, consistent quality, " Mr. Rock said.
(MarijuanaNews note: That is nice, but right now people are able to get medical marijuana of " consistent quality " at the compassion clubs. Does Rock think that everyone who needs medical marijuana is going to jump through his hoops?)
See
One Of The 20 Legal Canadian Medical Marijuana Patients Demands That Government Supply Him With His Medicine – More Pressure on Health Canada

" And by this time next year, clinical trials will be within full swing and we will be accumulating scientific evidence about the comparative medical implications of smoking marijuana for the alleviation of symptoms in the alleviation of chronic and other diseases. "
See
Health Canada To Spend Five Years and Millions
Playing the Research Game Trying Avoid Medical Marijuana

Mr. Rock said that no patient whose application showed they could benefit from marijuana has been rejected.

" Not so much rejected, but some people's applications were not complete. We had a lot of one-page letters from people saying, 'Please send me dope.' Those did not make the cut, " he said.

" Will the day ever come when it's available on pharmacists' shelves? " asked Mr. Rock.

" Marinol, a pill form of THC, is already available on druggists' shelves. So the day may come, " he said.
See
Marinol Was The First Schedule 2 Drug To Be " Down-Scheduled, "
Boasts Roxanne On Its New Marinol.com Web Site.
Doesn’t That Mean That It Should Never Have Been Schedule 2 Anyway?

" I think these are all mechanical consequences that follow from a basic decision: Are you going to let someone in pain have access to a drug they think will alleviate it? " he asked. " Yes, we've decided that. "

" There was never a good answer as to why it wasn't medically available, " added Mr. Rock.
(MarijuanaNews note: Excuse me! Alan Rock is Health Minister. But he is right. We have never had a good answer from him about why he has delayed medical marijuana.)

" My mother was on morphine for a month before she died, and yet morphine is considered a prohibited drug. It's criminalized, people traffic in it and go to jail, and yet the doctor prescribed it and we had it in the room. She died at home, and we had it in the house. "
(MarijuanaNews note: What if Rock’s mother had needed medical marijuana?)
See
 " Rock keeps talking about doing trials, but trials have already been done. There is already sufficient proof that cannabis helps people deal with their pain. " -- Ontario Arthritic Facing Marijuana Charge.
" My death will be slow and painful. Now, I have this criminal charge against me,
and my children are about to lose their daddy over it. "
and
Scathing Column In Ottawa Citizen Attacks Health Minister’s Rationing Of Medical Marijuana...
And Justice.
